findings.text: NOT_ADMISSIBLE_PHASES re-spells the pair that WAITING_UPSTREAM_PHASES already owns at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:81, whose comment says the two are declared there 'rather than spelled out at each filter'; _stall_stage at :1419 still spells the same pair inline, so one fact now has three spellings in one module and a phase added to one leaves the stall rule's suppression and the stage derivation disagreeing.

HOLD_VERDICTS enumerates the same seven hold words that reckon/crew/runs.py:2110 _DRAIN_STUCK_VERDICTS already enumerates as its queued subset; a hold word added at a write site has to be added to both sets and nothing fails when it is added to only one, so a new hold would either keep a request stalling or drop it from the drain view's stuck rule.

the hold cases are parametrised over `sorted(queue_admission.HOLD_VERDICTS)` and the phase case at :276 over NOT_ADMISSIBLE_PHASES, so the test's input set is the production constant itself: dropping a word from that set deletes the case silently instead of failing, which is the one regression this guard cannot see.

baseline_suite names tests/test_a_refusal_at_admission_is_routed.py while after_suite (line 24) names tests/test_the_queue_reports_its_own_stalls.py, so the recorded arms are not one template resolved over each tree and the pair cannot be read as a same-gate delta; the reproduction it carries (test_a_request_no_lane_fits_is_held_naming_the_shortfall red at 0533fe80dc) is real and belongs under artifacts rather than in the base arm.
